did_you_know.text: Moses conveys these words to the Israelites as the Lord commanded, emphasizing that the laws in the chapter are divine commands delivered through him.
The command is given to the heads of the tribes and begins with the words “This is the word,” emphasizing the importance and authority of the message.
The chapter teaches the importance of keeping one’s word: anyone who makes a vow or swears an oath must fulfill everything he has spoken and must not break his word.
When a young woman is living in her father’s house, her father’s silence on the day he hears her vow or binding obligation allows them to remain in force.
A father may disallow his daughter’s vow on the day he hears it. In that case, her vows and binding obligations do not remain in force, and the verse says that the Lord will forgive her.
The vows of a widow or a divorced woman remain binding on her, unlike cases in which Scripture describes a father or husband having authority to intervene in a vow.
Regarding a married woman, Scripture explains that her husband can confirm or annul a vow or an oath of obligation, especially vows involving self-denial.
If a husband hears the vow and remains silent day after day, his silence is considered confirmation of the vows or binding obligations, and they remain in force.
If he later annuls the vow after hearing it, he bears responsibility for the woman’s guilt.
At the end of the chapter, Scripture summarizes that these laws concern the relationship between a man and his wife and between a father and his daughter during her youth in her father’s house.
